memory_update.text: Olo remains one of the cleanest comps for restaurant ordering, delivery integration, payments, and guest engagement, but it is no longer a US-listed candidate after the September 12, 2025 Thoma Bravo acquisition and NYSE delisting.

PAR Technology should be carried forward as the highest-purity underfollowed public candidate for this node because it combines POS, Punchh loyalty/engagement, PAR Ordering/MENU, delivery, payments, and restaurant operating software.
NCR Voyix is a messy-label small-cap infrastructure candidate: legacy POS/retail turnaround optics may obscure restaurant Aloha, kitchen, loyalty, online ordering, and payment modernization exposure.
Shift4 is a less pure but plausible second-order restaurant channel-infrastructure candidate through SkyTab, hospitality payment volume, online ordering, loyalty, and integrated payment acceptance.

For restaurant brands, the chokepoint is not only delivery demand but control of the customer relationship: first-party ordering, loyalty identity, payment data, kitchen routing, and POS integration can shift economics away from aggregator dependency.

node: Delivery channel infrastructure, ordering platforms, loyalty, and customer data
summary: This pass expands the public-company universe around the chokepoint that restaurants need direct digital ordering, loyalty, payments, POS, kitchen routing, and customer-data infrastructure to reduce margin leakage to third-party aggregators. The strongest pure-play public reference, Olo, is no longer eligible as a US-listed candidate because Thoma Bravo completed its acquisition in September 2025 and Olo's shares ceased trading. The remaining US-listed map is therefore split between a high-attention restaurant-tech reference leader, Toast, and underfollowed/smaller infrastructure names such as PAR Technology, NCR Voyix, and Shift4, which sit in POS, engagement, ordering, kitchen workflow, payment acceptance, and restaurant operating-system layers.
